diagnostic_command: python -m pytest -s -q <isolated-tree>/tests/test_bridge_mac_integration.py::test_real_macs_sustain_bidirectional_ipv4_bursts_above_500_mbps -x; the temporary copy sets sys_half_period_ns to 10 for 50 MHz or 4 for 125 MHz and prints the captured output counts, counters, window, and per-direction rate.

stimulus.directions: Concurrent SFP0-to-SFP1 and SFP1-to-SFP0 physical RX streams
stimulus.schedule: Six valid IPv4 frames, then one IPv6 and one corrupt-FCS IPv4; repeated six times, so a valid frame follows each rejected pair.
stimulus.phy_clock: 125 MHz asynchronous RX/TX clocks with independent phase offsets
stimulus.system_clock: 50 MHz (10 ns half-period) or 125 MHz (4 ns half-period)
stimulus.bounded_window: From burst start to 8192 system-clock cycles after both input bursts finish; duration is read from Verilator simulation time.
stimulus.rate_definition: Per-direction successfully captured Ethernet payload bits divided by the measured bounded window; preamble and FCS excluded. Output equality is asserted before the 500 Mbps threshold.

results.validation: Failed exact output comparison: each path transmitted only 8 of 36 expected valid frames (28 missing per path).
Failed exact output comparison: 36 of the 72 expected valid frames were transmitted; the bridge reported 18 queue-busy overflows per path.

Below the target and incomplete. The bridge counters account for 23 of 48 frames per input direction; 25 are missing before the bridge stream counters. The simulation exposes MAC CRC counters but no dedicated MAC CDC/drop counter, so the upstream loss location is inferred, not directly counted.

All 36 complete physical IPv4 output frames per direction exactly matched the expected preamble, frame bytes, and independently generated zlib FCS; IPv6 and corrupt-FCS frames produced no output. Both directions exceeded 500 Mbps.

limits: The simulated Mbps is physical-MAC-seam payload throughput, not host TCP throughput or board qualification.
The 500 Mbps assertion is applied only to the 125 MHz system-clock configuration; the 50 MHz configuration is retained for diagnostic comparison.
